features.name: allow_fail
features.reason: removed due to no clear use cases

features.name: const_compare_raw_pointers
features.reason: cannot be allowed in const eval in any meaningful way

features.name: const_in_array_repeat_expressions
features.reason: removed due to causing promotable bugs

features.name: const_raw_ptr_to_usize_cast
features.reason: at compile-time, pointers do not have an integer value, so these casts cannot be properly supported

features.name: const_trait_bound_opt_out
features.reason: Removed in favor of `[const]` bound in #![feature(const_trait_impl)]

features.name: default_type_parameter_fallback
features.reason: never properly implemented; requires significant design work

features.name: deprecated_safe
features.reason: never properly implemented, in the way of attribute refactor

features.name: dyn_compatible_for_dispatch
features.reason: removed, not used heavily and represented additional complexity in dyn compatibility

features.name: dyn_star
features.reason: removed as it was no longer necessary for AFIDT (async fn in dyn trait) support

features.name: external_doc
features.reason: use #[doc = include_str!("filename")] instead, which handles macro invocations

features.name: ffi_returns_twice
features.reason: being investigated by the ffi-unwind project group

features.name: in_band_lifetimes
features.reason: removed due to unsolved ergonomic questions and added lifetime resolution complexity

features.name: infer_static_outlives_requirements
features.reason: removed as it caused some confusion and discussion was inactive for years

features.name: inline_const_pat
features.reason: removed due to implementation concerns as it requires significant refactorings

features.name: link_args
features.reason: removed in favor of using `-C link-arg=ARG` on command line, \ which is available from cargo build scripts with `cargo:rustc-link-arg` now

features.name: min_type_alias_impl_trait
features.reason: removed in favor of full type_alias_impl_trait

features.name: never_type_fallback
features.reason: removed in favor of unconditional fallback

features.name: no_debug
features.reason: removed due to lack of demand

features.name: platform_intrinsics
features.reason: SIMD intrinsics use the regular intrinsics ABI now

features.name: precise_pointer_size_matching
features.reason: removed in favor of half-open ranges

features.name: pref_align_of
features.reason: removed due to marginal use and inducing compiler complications

features.name: pub_macro_rules
features.reason: removed due to being incomplete, in particular it does not work across crates

features.name: rust_2018_preview
features.reason: 2018 Edition preview is no longer relevant

features.name: start
features.reason: not portable enough and never RFC'd

features.name: target_feature_inline_always
features.reason: removed because of unfixable soundness issues

features.name: unsized_locals
features.reason: removed due to implementation concerns; see https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/111942

features.name: unsized_tuple_coercion
features.reason: The feature restricts possible layouts for tuples, and this restriction is not worth it.

features.name: untagged_unions
features.reason: unions with `Copy` and `ManuallyDrop` fields are stable; there is no intent to stabilize more

features.name: wasm_abi
features.reason: non-standard wasm ABI is no longer supported

unsafe_attributes.note: the `#[naked]` attribute adds the safety obligation that the function's body must respect the function’s calling convention, uphold its signature, and either return or diverge (i.e., not fall through past the end of the assembly code).
a function with the signature of the function the attribute is applied to must only be callable if the force-enabled features are guaranteed to be present
the linker's behavior with multiple libraries exporting duplicate symbol names is undefined and Rust cannot provide guarantees when you manually override them
the program's behavior with overridden link sections on items is unpredictable and Rust cannot provide guarantees when you manually override them

`#[ffi_const]` functions shall have no effects except for its return value, which can only depend on the values of the function parameters, and is not affected by changes to the observable state of the program.
`#[ffi_pure]` functions shall have no effects except for its return value, which shall not change across two consecutive function calls with the same parameters.
the linker's behavior with multiple libraries exporting duplicate symbol names is undefined and Rust cannot provide guarantees when you manually override them

            the implementations of the trait are not considered when specializing
